cards.q: What is IGMP and what does it do on the LAN?
cards.a: IGMP is the host-to-router protocol that manages multicast group membership on a LAN segment at the Layer 2/3 boundary. Routers use it to learn which groups hosts want to receive, and without members the router stops forwarding the group's traffic.

cards.q: Which IGMP version is the default, and what does IGMPv3 add?
cards.a: IGMPv2 is the default; IGMPv3 adds source-specific include/exclude filtering, which is required for SSM.

cards.q: How do IGMPv1, v2, and v3 differ?
cards.a: v1 uses general queries with a slow leave (about 2 minutes) and no SSM; v2 adds a fast leave-group message; v3 supports source-specific reports with include/exclude source lists, enabling SSM.

cards.q: What are the roles on an IGMP segment, and who wins the querier election?
cards.a: The querier is the elected router that sends general queries, members are hosts that send reports, and non-members stay silent. One querier per LAN is elected, and the lowest IP address wins.

cards.q: What destination address do general IGMP queries use?
Where do IGMPv2 and v3 reports go?
cards.a: Reports are multicast to 224.0.0.22, used by both v2 and v3.

cards.q: What destination address does an IGMPv2 leave message use?
How does a host stay an active IGMP member?
cards.a: The host keeps sending reports; no report means the router times the host out and removes its membership.

cards.q: What does ip pim sparse-mode do for IGMP on an interface?
cards.a: It enables both PIM and IGMP on the interface.

cards.q: Which commands force IGMPv3, make the router join a group, and create static membership?
cards.a: ip igmp version 3 forces v3 (SSM-ready), ip igmp join-group makes the router join a group for testing, and ip igmp static-group creates static membership.

cards.q: What is IGMP snooping, and what is an mrouter port?
cards.a: IGMP snooping is a switch feature that inspects IGMP reports so group traffic is forwarded only to member ports instead of being flooded to all ports; the mrouter port is the port that faces the router.

cards.q: Which commands verify IGMP groups, IGMP interfaces, and snooping?
cards.a: show ip igmp groups shows learned groups, show ip igmp interface shows per-interface IGMP status, and show ip igmp snooping groups verifies snooping on the switch; show ip mroute tracks the multicast tree.

cards.q: On a router with no IGMP groups listed at all, what is the likely cause?
cards.a: PIM is not enabled on the interface; check with show ip igmp interface.

cards.q: Multicast group traffic is flooding to all switch ports; what is likely wrong?
cards.a: IGMP snooping is disabled on the switch; check with show ip igmp snooping.

cards.q: Is IGMP a router-to-router multicast routing protocol?
cards.a: No. IGMP covers host-to-router membership only, on the LAN side at the Layer 2/3 boundary; it is not used between routers.

cards.q: Which IGMP version provides fast leave, and how?
cards.a: IGMPv2 sends an explicit leave-group message to 224.0.0.2, speeding up removal versus v1's slow timeout-based leave.
